the development of an environmentally safe wheyer protein-based adhesive that has excellent water resistance and low formaldehyde emission.
the development of a water-resistant whey protein-based wood adhesive that can be used in the manufacture of water-resistant wood products.

the post-treated PFO-modified water-resistant whey protein-based wood adhesive has a great potential to be a good alternative to the conventional phenol-formaldehyde-based wood adhesives.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the post-treated phenol-formaldehyde oligomers with low molecular weight and low viscosity are suitable to modify whey protein-based wood adhesive to improve water resistance and to reduce formaldehyde emission, and ammonia-sulfite scavenging is an efficient method to further decrease the formaldehyde emission.
whey protein adhesion is a good alternative to urea formaldehyde and phenol formaldehyde adhesives in plywood manufacturing.
the post-treatment of PFO can be used to modify whey protein-based wood adhesives, and the combination of ammonia and sodium hydroxide is the most preferable to the PFO post-treatments.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the whey protein-based water-resistant adhesive modified by the low-molecular-weight phenol-formaldehyde oligomer (PFO) with a low content catalyst (NaOH) and low reaction temperature (75oC) is environmentally safe and has good bond properties.
the PFO post-treated whey protein-based wood adhesive is a promising alternative to the conventional phenol-formaldehyde resin-based wood adhesives.
a low-molecular PFO synthesized at a low reaction condition can be used as a modifier for whey protein-based wood adhesives to reduce formaldehyde emissions and to improve water resistance.
